question.value: What are the H$_2$ number density and kinetic temperature of molecular clouds in the vicinity of the LMC supernova remnant N49, and are they heated by supernova shocks or cosmic rays?

evidence.quote: In this paper, we derive the H$_2$ number density and kinetic temperature of molecular clouds in the vicinity of the SNR N49 using ALMA observations of $^{12}$CO($J$ = 1–0, 2–1, 3–2) and $^{13}$CO($J$ = 2–1) and a non-LTE analysis.

analysis_steps.goal: Derive kinetic temperature and H2 number density via non-LTE LVG analysis

method.value: Perform non-LTE radiative transfer calculations using the Large Velocity Gradient (LVG) approximation on 12CO(2-1), 12CO(3-2), and 13CO(2-1) line intensities for each of the eight clouds

evidence.quote: Using $^{12}$CO($J$ = 2–1, 3–2) and $^{13}$CO($J$ = 2–1) line emission data taken with the Atacama Large Millimeter/Submillimeter Array, we derived the H$_2$ number density and kinetic temperature of eight $^{13}$CO-detected clouds using the large velocity gradient approximation

In order to estimate the kinetic temperature $T_\mathrm{kin}$ and H$_2$ number density $n$(H$_2$) of molecular clouds in N49, we performed a non-LTE analysis using the large velocity gradient (LVG) approximation (cite: 1974ApJ...189..441G; 1974ApJ...187L..67S).
The $^{12}$CO($J$ =1–0) data were not included in the LVG analysis because the lowest-$J$ transition may be subject to self-absorption owing to a large optical depth (cite: 2010PASJ...62...51M).

key_parameters.value: Individual velocity gradient dv/dr calculated for each cloud from HMHW linewidth dv and cloud radius dr

evidence.quote: Here, $dv$ is the half-maximum half-width (HMHW) linewidth of the CO line profile derived by least-squares fitting with a Gaussian kernel, and $dr$ is the cloud radius.
Since the eight molecular clouds have different cloud sizes and linewidths, we calculated individual $dv/dr$ for each cloud.

assumptions.value: Isothermal spherical cloud with uniform photon escape probability and velocity gradient dv/dr

evidence.quote: This non-LTE code calculates the radiative transfer of multiple transitions of atomic and/or molecular lines, assuming an isothermal spherical cloud with uniform photon escape probability and velocity gradient of $dv/dr$.

We also used the abundance ratio of \[$^{12}$CO/H$_2$\]$~=~1.6 \times 10^{-5}$ and the abundance ratio of isotopes \[$^{12}$CO/$^{13}$CO\] = 50 (cite: 1987ApJ...315..621B; 2010PASJ...62...51M; 2011AJ....141...73M; 2014ApJ...796..123F).

findings_qualitative.value: The molecular clouds associated with SNR N49 fall into two groups: three shock-front clouds (K, L, T) with high kinetic temperatures (~42-46 K) and lower densities (~480-720 cm^-3), and five more distant clouds (N, O, P, Q, R) with moderate temperatures (~19-21 K) and higher densities (~780-1320 cm^-3).

evidence.quote: The physical properties of the clouds are divided into two categories: three of them near the shock front show the highest temperatures of $\sim$50 K with densities of $\sim$500–700 cm$^{-3}$, while other clouds slightly distant from the SNR have moderate temperatures of $\sim$20 K with densities of $\sim$800–1300 cm$^{-3}$.

findings_qualitative.value: Clouds K, L, and T are heated by supernova shocks, representing the first compelling evidence of shock-heated molecular clouds in an extragalactic SNR, consistent with thermal conduction producing X-ray recombining plasma.

evidence.quote: The former clouds were heated by supernova shocks, but the latter were dominantly affected by the cosmic-ray heating. These findings are consistent with the efficient production of X-ray recombining plasma in N49 due to thermal conduction between the cold clouds and hot plasma.
This is the first compelling evidence of shock-heated molecular clouds in an extragalactic SNR.

findings_qualitative.value: Clouds N, O, P, Q, and R lie along a constant-pressure relation (negative correlation between T_kin and n(H2)) and were not evaporated by shocks, whereas clouds K, L, and T are shifted to higher pressure and lower density, indicating partial shock evaporation.

evidence.quote: The negative correlation between $T_\mathrm{kin}$ and $n$(H$_2$) indicates that clouds N, O, P, Q, and R have constant pressure and did not experience shock evaporation within the short SNR age of $\sim$4800 yr.

On the other hand, clouds K, L, and T, which are on the inside or on the edge of the shell, are significantly shifted from this pressure-constant line to a higher-pressure region and have slightly reduced densities, suggesting that the shock-engulfed clouds were partially evaporated through the shock-cloud interaction.

claims.hypothesis: Molecular clouds interacting with the shock front of SNR N49 in the LMC are heated by supernova shocks rather than local stellar sources or cosmic rays alone.
claims.experiment: Perform non-LTE LVG radiative transfer analysis using ALMA 12CO(J=2-1, 3-2) and 13CO(J=2-1) line intensities at 3.5'' resolution for eight 13CO-detected clouds and compare with radial distance from the SNR shell and cosmic-ray diffusion/PDR models.
claims.result: Clouds K, L, and T on or inside the shock front have T_kin ~ 42-46 K and n(H2) ~ 480-720 cm^-3, whereas pre-shocked/ambient clouds N, O, P, Q, and R have T_kin ~ 19-21 K and n(H2) ~ 780-1320 cm^-3; cosmic-ray diffusion length is ~6 pc (reaching all clouds equally).
claims.finding: The high kinetic temperatures of clouds K, L, and T are caused by supernova shock heating, providing the first compelling evidence of shock-heated molecular clouds associated with an extragalactic SNR.

evidence.quote: three of them near the shock front show the highest temperatures of $\sim$50 K with densities of $\sim$500–700 cm$^{-3}$, while other clouds slightly distant from the SNR have moderate temperatures of $\sim$20 K with densities of $\sim$800–1300 cm$^{-3}$.
In other words, cosmic-ray heating is not sufficient to increase the kinetic temperature of K, L, and T significantly above those of the unshocked clouds (O, Q, R, etc).

Since the spatial variation of $T_\mathrm{kin}$ cannot be explained by cosmic-ray heating alone or extra heating sources like O-type stars, we conclude that the high $T_\mathrm{kin}$ values of the clouds were caused by supernova shocks.

claims.hypothesis: The moderate kinetic temperatures (~20 K) of the unshocked/ambient clouds (N, O, P, Q, R) near SNR N49 are caused by cosmic-ray heating from particles accelerated in the SNR.
claims.experiment: Calculate the cosmic-ray diffusion length for 100 MeV protons over the SNR age and simulate the time evolution of cloud center gas temperature using a 1D plane-parallel PDR model with enhanced cosmic-ray ionization rates.
claims.result: The cosmic-ray diffusion length is l_diff ~ 6 pc (exceeding the distance to cloud P), and PDR modeling shows that cosmic-ray ionization rates 30-300 times the standard Galactic value reproduce T_kin ~ 20 K.
claims.finding: Cosmic-ray heating naturally explains the moderate ~20 K temperatures of the pre-shocked and ambient molecular clouds surrounding N49.

evidence.quote: Adopting $t_\mathrm{age} = 1.5 \times 10^{11}$ s (cite: 2012ApJ...748..117P), $E = 100$ MeV, and $B = 10~\mu$G, we obtain $l_\mathrm{diff} \sim$6 pc which is substantially larger than the maximum separation between cloud P and the shock boundary of the SNR.

Since the typical cosmic-ray ionization rates in the vicinity of Galactic SNRs are $\sim$30–300 times higher than the standard Galactic value of $\sim$$10^{-17}$ s$^{-1}$ (cite: 2010ApJ...724.1357I; 2011ApJ...740L...4C; 2014A&A...568A..50V), the observed values of $T_\mathrm{kin}$ $\sim$20 K at pre-shocked and ambient clouds can be explained as the cosmic-ray heating effect.

claims.hypothesis: Dense clumpy molecular clouds inside a low-density stellar wind bubble survive complete shock destruction over the ~4800 yr age of SNR N49, with only shock-engulfed clouds experiencing partial evaporation.
claims.experiment: Analyze the correlation between T_kin and n(H2) across the eight clouds using MPFITEXY and estimate the shock cloud-crossing timescale for a density contrast of 10^5.
claims.result: Clouds N, O, P, Q, and R follow a negative T_kin-n(H2) correlation indicating constant thermal pressure, while shock-engulfed clouds K, L, and T are shifted to higher pressures and lower densities (~480-720 cm^-3); the shock cloud-crossing time is ~10^5 yr >> 4800 yr.
claims.finding: Clouds N, O, P, Q, and R have not undergone shock evaporation, whereas shock-engulfed clouds K, L, and T were partially evaporated on their surfaces through shock-cloud interactions.

evidence.quote: Adopting the density contrast $n_\mathrm{cloud} / n_0 = 10^5$, $V_\mathrm{sh} = 3000$ km s$^{-1}$, and a cloud radius of 1 pc, the cloud-crossing time of supernova shocks is $\sim$$10^5$ yr, and hence the cloud can survive the shock destruction within the typical lifetime of a SNR (cite: 2021Ap&SS.366...58S).

The negative correlation between $T_\mathrm{kin}$ and $n$(H$_2$) indicates that clouds N, O, P, Q, and R have constant pressure and did not experience shock evaporation within the short SNR age of $\sim$4800 yr.

On the other hand, clouds K, L, and T, which are on the inside or on the edge of the shell, are significantly shifted from this pressure-constant line to a higher-pressure region and have slightly reduced densities, suggesting that the shock-engulfed clouds were partially evaporated through the shock-cloud interaction.

why_this_data.value: N49 in the LMC is associated with molecular clouds and has a known distance and very little line-of-sight contamination; multi-transition CO and 13CO ALMA observations resolve sub-parsec clouds and enable non-LTE temperature and density determinations.

evidence.quote: On the other hand, there have been no such studies on extragalactic SNRs especially in the Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC), despite the advantages of very little contamination along the line of sight (cite: 2010A&A...520A..24S) and its known distance (cite: 2013Natur.495...76P).

LHA 120-N49 (hereafter N49) in the LMC is one of the best extragalactic SNRs to study shock-heating and compression of a gaseous medium because it is believed to be associated with molecular clouds (cite: 1997ApJ...480..607B; 2010AJ....139...68V; 2015ApJ...808...77U).

why_this_method.value: Non-LTE Large Velocity Gradient (LVG) analysis of multiple CO transitions and 13CO(2-1) constrains both kinetic temperature and H2 density, while excluding 12CO(1-0) avoids self-absorption bias at large optical depth.

evidence.quote: In order to estimate the kinetic temperature $T_\mathrm{kin}$ and H$_2$ number density $n$(H$_2$) of molecular clouds in N49, we performed a non-LTE analysis using the large velocity gradient (LVG) approximation (cite: 1974ApJ...189..441G; 1974ApJ...187L..67S).
The $^{12}$CO($J$ =1–0) data were not included in the LVG analysis because the lowest-$J$ transition may be subject to self-absorption owing to a large optical depth (cite: 2010PASJ...62...51M).

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Heating by local OB stars or young stellar objects was rejected because no such extra heating sources are associated with the molecular clouds near N49.

evidence.quote: It is noteworthy that no extra heating sources such as OB stars and/or young stellar objects are associated with the molecular clouds in the vicinity of the SNR.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Cosmic-ray heating alone as the cause of the ~40-50 K temperatures in clouds K, L, and T was rejected because the ~6 pc cosmic-ray diffusion length means cosmic rays heat all clouds equally.

evidence.quote: In other words, cosmic-ray heating is not sufficient to increase the kinetic temperature of K, L, and T significantly above those of the unshocked clouds (O, Q, R, etc).

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Including 12CO(J=1-0) in the LVG analysis was rejected due to potential self-absorption from high optical depth.

evidence.quote: The $^{12}$CO($J$ =1–0) data were not included in the LVG analysis because the lowest-$J$ transition may be subject to self-absorption owing to a large optical depth (cite: 2010PASJ...62...51M).

limitations_admitted.value: Decomposing the density and velocity distribution of the shocked clouds K, L, and T requires even higher-angular-resolution observations.

evidence.quote: Quantifying this scenario requires a decomposition of the density and velocity distribution of clouds K, L and T which requires even higher-resolution data (cite: 2021MNRAS.500.1721M; 2022MNRAS.509.2180S).

limitations_admitted.value: Projection effects affect the apparent radial distances of clouds O, Q, and R relative to cloud K.

evidence.quote: Although clouds O, Q, and R have smaller radial distances than cloud K, this is likely due to projection effects.

limitations_admitted.value: Confirming the thermal conduction origin of the X-ray recombining plasma requires higher angular and spectral resolution X-ray spectroscopy (e.g., Athena, XRISM).

evidence.quote: Additional spatially resolved X-ray spectroscopy with high-angular/spectral resolution is needed to confirm this scenario. The Athena mission has the potential to accomplish these (cite: 2013arXiv1306.2307N).

limitations_admitted.value: Directly estimating the cosmic-ray ionization rate in N49 requires follow-up observations of lines such as HCO+, DCO+, and/or [CI].

evidence.quote: Further follow-up observations using multiple emission lines such as HCO$^{+}$, DCO$^{+}$ (cite: 2014A&A...568A..50V), and/or \[Ci\] (cite: 2023arXiv230615983Y) are needed to estimate the cosmic-ray ionization rate in the vicinity of the LMC SNR N49.

referee_caveats_inferred: The LVG analysis relies on fixed assumed abundance ratios ([12CO/H2] = 1.6e-5 and [12CO/13CO] = 50) for all clouds, whereas selective photodissociation or shock chemistry could alter the [12CO/13CO] ratio in the shock-front clouds K, L, and T (which have weak 13CO detections and large T_kin uncertainties, e.g., 46 +57/-18 K for cloud T).

12CO(3-2) was observed only with the 7 m + TP arrays (3.48'' x 2.76'' beam), whereas 12CO(2-1) and 13CO(2-1) were observed with 12 m + 7 m arrays without Total Power data, potentially introducing differential spatial filtering of extended emission despite smoothing to 3.5''.
